overview: This single-page administrative list of papers for State Department File No. 894.71294A concerns the transportation of foreign mail between Japan and Taiwan (then commonly called Formosa). It indexes one report, dated October 18 but without a stated year, on the inauguration of a preliminary weekly airmail service between the two territories and supplies a related file reference, S.E. 894.79694a/1.

subfiles.summary: The page is the list of papers for File No. 894.71294A. It identifies one item, apparently originating in Teihoku and dated October 18, concerning the inauguration of preliminary weekly airmail service between Japan and Taiwan. It also provides the associated reference S.E. 894.79694a/1; no year, recipient, or full underlying report is present in the supplied text.

interest: The page is useful as a concise archival locator for evidence about the early development of scheduled aviation and postal links between metropolitan Japan and colonial Taiwan. Its simultaneous use of “Formosa” and “Taiwan,” together with the Japanese-period place-name rendered by OCR as “Teihoku,” also illustrates the shifting geographical terminology encountered in American diplomatic records. The related-file reference may help a historian locate the substantive report indexed here.
